<!-- pr-reviewer: ee0405765843355dff71e1add7ecdceffd8166e9 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge, after #2112 (stacked; reviewed as its last commit against its parent). No blocking findings; two non-blocking notes on the load margin and the commit type.

Safety floor (toolpath): read as a safety review, built and run locally on m5 (rules from `upstream/main:AGENTS.md`).

**What looks good**
- The retrace never leaves legal, load-read space. In `rest/pass.rs` `attempt` every lead, the retrace included, is asked the same three checks over its whole `pts`: every chord inside the center area (`wall_chord`/`chord_clears`), the verifier's crossing law against the depth's earlier feeds, and `walk_until` on the conservative stock raster against the planner bound. The retrace is `done` (the chords of the pass just cut) reversed, plus at most a wall ride between two canon vertices (`wall_between`, capped at 3 diameters, 4096 vertices), so it can only be over cut floor or the same wall stretch the old lead already rode. If a wall ride touched unproved stock, the load walk reads it and refuses the lead. It is a feed at cut depth and never a plunge, so the entry guard is untouched. `retrace` returns `None` for a closed run, a stale `done` (`done.last() != cur`), a different wall loop, or past 8 diameters; `pts.len() - 1` and `pts[run_at.min(len)..]` cannot panic on a non-empty `done`.
- The cells cannot leave slivers. `TILE_PER_D` only changes which cell a run is started from (`rounds`' `here` filter): `runs()` is still computed on the whole remaining material, never clipped to the cell, so nothing falls between cells. Coverage is still the final `p.goal.standing()` against `COVER_MAX`, which refuses by name (`cannot prove its coverage`) if anything is left. Cell edges are on the area bbox grown by a full diameter. A degenerate (NaN) bbox yields zero cells and is then refused by that same coverage check.
- Mutations (local): without the retrace (`out.extend(self.retrace(run))` removed) four rest_adaptive tests go red, with the corner and neck plans refused by the budget ("479 mm out of cut for 117 mm in cut" and "1553 for 467") and the island at 1035 air for 494 cut, as claimed. With the cells off (`TILE_PER_D` 1e6) the neck is refused: "22 passes by a retract (over 16 ...)", as claimed.
- The budget refuses by name with the fix ("choose Waterline or Offset rings"). `cut_count` guards non-finite input and the casts; no new unwrap/expect/panic outside tests. Provenance lines present; files under ~400 lines (peel.rs 359, leads.rs 339). Decision record present. No dependency, script, workflow, goldens, snapshot or process-file change.

**Results (locally, m5, PR head; GitHub reports MERGEABLE)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib -- adaptive`: 76 passed, 6 ignored
- `--test rest_adaptive`: 9 passed (35 s); `rest2d`: 10; `adaptive_hsm`: 1 passed, 5 ignored; `optimal_load`: 4; `machining2d`: 66
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- (The 11-test count with #2114's tests is not here: this PR is not stacked on #2114.)

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. Neck load, 15.376% of D against a limit of 15.377%. I reproduced it (printed per depth: corner 14.72%, island 13.13%, neck before this PR 15.05%, neck now 15.3760%). It is not a fixture tuned to pass: the limit is the planner's own cap (`optimal` 14.645% x `1 + PLAN_TOL` 1.05 = 15.3773%), and the planner raises each pass up its step ladder until it reaches that cap, so a fixture whose cut reaches the ladder's top reads at the cap by construction (the cell-boundary pass, per the record). The margin is real, though, and it is 0.0013% of D. Two things follow. (a) The test's limit is the planner's limit with no headroom of its own, so a platform whose float or libm differs in the last digit (Linux runner, Windows) can read 15.378% and fail with nothing wrong; this is the kind of per-OS reading AGENTS.md warns about, and none of the platforms but macOS has run it. (b) A coarser measuring grid reads higher (#2114 shows D/80 at x1.2). I would give the neck assertion a stated headroom of its own (for example a `LOAD_SLACK` of 0.055 for this fixture, or a comment naming 15.377% as the cap) rather than change the planner's 5%.
2. Travel budget: 3.0x out of cut against 2.6x to 2.8x read on the fixtures is just above them, and the hop budget (16 for 9 used on the neck) is looser. The pins `r.air <= 2.0/1.5/1.6 * r.cut` are on a cut figure that the record says is inflated by wall contact, so they bind less than they read. All of these are guard rails on a refuse-only path, so I leave them.
3. Moves rose 3216 -> 4064 and 14850 -> 17840 (chords; arc fit not started), disclosed. Planning time about the same.
4. The commit is typed `fix` and the body says `Fixes #2109`, but #2109 is labelled `enhancement` (P7) and changes behaviour of an unmerged `feat`. As it is stacked on #2112 (a `feat` waiting for its cut) it cannot merge before it anyway; a `feat(motion)` or `perf` subject on the PR title/merge commit would keep it from being read as a mid-cycle fix merge by `/merge-ready`.
5. `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs` ends with a new blank line (rustfmt nit).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
